title: Nvidia's Rubin CPX Back From the Dead? Ming-Chi Kuo Says AI Chip Back With Major Redesign

questions.question: Will NVIDIA begin production of the redesigned Rubin CPX accelerator by March 31, 2027?
questions.why_it_matters: Rubin CPX is described as a redesigned accelerator for AI-inference prefill, intended to work alongside Vera Rubin systems rather than replace them. If produced, it could add a distinct product to NVIDIA’s data-center offering and potentially support sales of broader systems. The article does not quantify revenue or confirm the production plan, so this is a product milestone to monitor, not a revenue forecast.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing Vera Rubin questions track sampling and customer shipments of Vera Rubin systems, while other questions track Rubin Ultra and other product milestones. Rubin CPX is a different accelerator, with a separate design and production timeline; whether it enters production can change independently of those outcomes.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check by March 31, 2027, an analyst check date corresponding to the end of the calendar first quarter cited in the article; the article does not state an exact production date beyond “1Q27.” Review NVIDIA announcements, product materials, earnings statements, and filings for confirmation that production began. The production timing is an attributed claim by analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, not a company-confirmed plan in this article.

evidence.quote: Now, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says the chip giant has revived the accelerator with a substantially redesigned architecture and plans to begin production in the first quarter of 2027.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article’s central evidence for a distinct CPX production milestone and its expected timing. This is attributed to analyst Ming-Chi Kuo, not confirmed by NVIDIA.

evidence.quote: “Just as the market had come to believe that Rubin CPX had been dropped from Nvidia's product roadmap,” Kuo said Monday in a post on X, adding that his latest industry checks indicate that Nvidia has “revived the program.”
evidence.what_it_shows: Kuo’s reported industry checks support the claim that the program has resumed, while the phrasing makes clear this is an analyst’s report rather than an official company announcement.

evidence.quote: Kuo said the new version is designed to deliver stronger prefill performance, with major changes to both its GPU specifications and rack architecture.
evidence.what_it_shows: The reported redesign and intended performance improvement suggest CPX is a materially distinct product configuration, rather than merely another name for Vera Rubin shipments.

evidence.quote: Rubin CPX is designed to accelerate the prefill stage of AI inference — the process of reading and processing a model's input before it generates a response.
evidence.what_it_shows: Explains the accelerator’s targeted workload and why it could add a distinct capability to NVIDIA’s AI-inference offering.

evidence.quote: Kuo said the accelerator will feature 168GB of HBM4 high-bandwidth memory per GPU, compared with 288GB of HBM4 memory in Nvidia's Rubin GPUs and 128GB of GDDR7 memory in the earlier CPX design.
evidence.what_it_shows: Reports specific hardware changes in the revived design, while distinguishing it from both Rubin GPUs and the earlier CPX design.

evidence.quote: The revived CPX will move into a standalone MGX ETL rack instead of sharing a rack with Rubin GPUs, according to Kuo.
evidence.what_it_shows: The reported standalone rack design further distinguishes CPX’s planned configuration from Vera Rubin systems.

evidence.quote: Customers could configure systems with 64, 128, 192 or 256 CPX GPUs.
evidence.what_it_shows: Provides reported configuration options that could matter to the product’s deployment flexibility; it does not establish that customers have ordered or deployed them.

evidence.quote: Within each 64-GPU module, eight compute trays would each house eight CPX GPUs, alongside a switch tray.
evidence.what_it_shows: Adds detail about the reported system architecture, but is not evidence of production having begun.

evidence.quote: Kuo also said Nvidia will use NVLink to connect the eight GPUs within each tray, while Ethernet will handle communication between trays and rack modules.
evidence.what_it_shows: Describes the reported interconnect design and supports treating the CPX architecture as a separate product milestone.

evidence.quote: Rather than replacing Rubin, CPX is expected to work alongside Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems.
evidence.what_it_shows: Explicitly distinguishes CPX from the Vera Rubin rollout tracked by existing questions; CPX is described as complementary, not the same shipment milestone.

evidence.quote: Kuo said Nvidia recommends a 1:1 ratio of CPX to Rubin GPUs, with CPX handling prefill and generating the KV cache before transferring that information to Rubin over Ethernet RDMA for the decode stage.
evidence.what_it_shows: Reports a proposed complementary role and ratio alongside Rubin GPUs, indicating potential relevance to system demand while remaining an attributed recommendation rather than confirmed sales or deployment.

evidence.quote: Just as the market had come to believe that Rubin CPX had been dropped from Nvidia's product roadmap, my latest industry checks indicate that Nvidia has revived the program, with production expected to begin in 1Q27.
evidence.what_it_shows: Kuo’s first-person statement reiterates the reported revival and expected production timing. It also underscores that the claim rests on his industry checks.

evidence.quote: Kuo's statement came after Nvidia appeared to remove CPX from its roadmap at GTC 2026, where the company instead highlighted Groq 3 LPUs and LPX racks.
evidence.what_it_shows: Provides context that CPX had appeared to be absent from NVIDIA’s roadmap at GTC 2026, which makes confirmation of renewed production an independently meaningful product milestone.

evidence.quote: Nvidia did not immediately respond to Benzinga's request for comment.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article reports no company confirmation of Kuo’s claim at publication time.

evidence.quote: In August, Nvidia reported $96.22 billion in second-quarter revenue, marking a 106% increase from a year earlier and surpassing the Street consensus estimate of $92.18 billion.
evidence.what_it_shows: Shows NVIDIA’s current reported revenue scale and growth, providing business context for a potentially additional product; it does not attribute any revenue to Rubin CPX.

evidence.quote: The company also said Vera Rubin was ramping into full production, with CoreWeave, Nebius, Microsoft Azure, Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud among its partners.
evidence.what_it_shows: Company-reported progress on the separate Vera Rubin platform provides context for potential complementary demand, but does not confirm CPX production.

questions_written.question: Will NVIDIA begin production of the redesigned Rubin CPX accelerator by March 31, 2027?

article:
Nvidia Corp's (NASDAQ: NVDA ) Rubin CPX appeared to have disappeared from the company's AI roadmap earlier this year. Now, analyst Ming-Chi Kuo says the chip giant has revived the accelerator with a substantially redesigned architecture and plans to begin production in the first quarter of 2027.
Ming-Chi Kuo Says Nvidia Has Revived Rubin CPX
"Just as the market had come to believe that Rubin CPX had been dropped from Nvidia's product roadmap," Kuo said Monday in a post on X , adding that his latest industry checks indicate that Nvidia has "revived the program."
Kuo said the new version is designed to deliver stronger prefill performance , with major changes to both its GPU specifications and rack architecture.
Rubin CPX is designed to accelerate the prefill stage of AI inference — the process of reading and processing a model's input before it generates a response.
Kuo said the accelerator will feature 168GB of HBM4 high-bandwidth memory per GPU, compared with 288GB of HBM4 memory in Nvidia's Rubin GPUs and 128GB of GDDR7 memory in the earlier CPX design.
The revived CPX will move into a standalone MGX ETL rack instead of sharing a rack with Rubin GPUs, according to Kuo.
Customers could configure systems with 64, 128, 192 or 256 CPX GPUs. Within each 64-GPU module, eight compute trays would each house eight CPX GPUs, alongside a switch tray.
Kuo also said Nvidia will use NVLink to connect the eight GPUs within each tray, while Ethernet will handle communication between trays and rack modules.
Rubin CPX Will Work Alongside Vera Rubin
Rather than replacing Rubin, CPX is expected to work alongside Nvidia's Vera Rubin NVL72 systems.
Kuo said Nvidia recommends a 1:1 ratio of CPX to Rubin GPUs, with CPX handling prefill and generating the KV cache before transferring that information to Rubin over Ethernet RDMA for the decode stage.
Just as the market had come to believe that Rubin CPX had been dropped from Nvidia's product roadmap, my latest industry checks indicate that Nvidia has revived the program, with production expected to begin in 1Q27. Compared with the previous design, the revived Rubin CPX…
Kuo's statement came after Nvidia appeared to remove CPX from its roadmap at GTC 2026 , where the company instead highlighted Groq 3 LPUs and LPX racks.
Nvidia did not immediately respond to Benzinga's request for comment.
Nvidia's Revenue Surges as Vera Rubin Ramps Up
In August, Nvidia reported $96.22 billion in second-quarter revenue , marking a 106% increase from a year earlier and surpassing the Street consensus estimate of $92.18 billion.
The company also said Vera Rubin was ramping into full production, with CoreWeave , Nebius , Microsoft Azure , Google Cloud and Oracle Cloud among its partners.
Price Action: Nvidia shares closed at $220.50 on Monday, up 1.36%. In after-hours trading, the shares are down 0.10%, according to Benzinga Pro.
According to Benzinga Edge Rankings , Nvidia ranks in the 98th percentile for growth and maintains positive price-trend ratings across the short-, medium- and long-term time frames.
